data.one_liner: Flutter-only drift implementation using sqflite for SQLite storage.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Drift database backend that runs on top of the sqflite plugin. It lets you write Drift tables and queries while storing data via sqflite’s file‑based SQLite. Ideal for projects that already use sqflite or are migrating from moor_flutter.
use_when: Migrating an existing moor_flutter project to Drift
You want a pure‑Flutter SQLite solution without native sqlite3 libs
You already depend on sqflite and prefer to keep a single storage plugin
avoid_when: Targeting web or desktop platforms where sqflite isn’t supported
Needing the highest possible SQLite performance provided by native libraries
strengths: No need for sqlite3_flutter_libs or other native binaries
weaknesses: Only supports Flutter platforms (android, ios, macos)
Relies on sqflite which can be slower than native sqlite3

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: Standard Drift setup using NativeDatabase for full native performance

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: Manual SQLite queries without Drift’s type‑safe API

alternatives.name: sqlite3
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides native SQLite bindings for higher performance
